questions.q: In the lesson's policy, what action results when only input drift is detected and AUC is still above its floor?
options: Retrain immediately
Investigate
Roll back to the previous model
Delete the monitoring data
questions.explain: Input drift is an early warning but often does not hurt accuracy, so the policy opens an investigation instead of an automatic rebuild.

questions.q: Why does the decision function check the cooldown first?
options: Cooldowns are cheaper to compute than AUC
Drift can only be measured after 14 days
The schedule trigger requires it
A freshly trained model should not be retrained again in a loop while its metrics settle
questions.explain: Without a cooldown, a noisy metric could cause back-to-back retrains. The cooldown caps how often the expensive action can fire.

questions.q: The policy has fired a performance trigger, but only 1,200 new labelled rows exist. What does the lesson's function return?
options: wait, because it needs at least 2000 labelled rows
retrain, because performance is the strongest signal
hold, because of the cooldown
investigate, because of drift
questions.explain: The volume rule prevents retraining on too little data. The policy waits until enough new labelled rows have arrived.

questions.q: The candidate scored 0.593 AUC against the champion's 0.529 on weeks 7 and 8, but the floor is 0.694. What is the right outcome?
options: Promote straight to production and close the alert
Discard the candidate because it is below the floor
Send the candidate to staging for review, and keep an investigation open because it is still below the floor
Lower the floor to 0.59
questions.explain: The candidate is meaningfully better, so it is worth reviewing, but it is still below the floor, which signals a deeper problem such as missing features.

questions.q: Why is the candidate evaluated on weeks 7 and 8 rather than on the weeks it was trained on?
options: Newer weeks are always easier to predict
A time-ordered split judges it on data newer than anything it learned from
The champion cannot be scored on older weeks
It makes the AUC number larger
questions.explain: Judging on later data mimics how the model will be used and avoids rewarding memorisation of the training weeks.
